headline: Benchmarking RNA-seq workflows for normalization, quality control, and sample size
label: Rna Sequencing Method Evaluation
summary: Recent preprints and papers assess RNA-seq and scRNA-seq methods against defined metrics, addressing cell calling, normalization, QC, and sample size.
synthesis: The common thread across these items is evaluation of RNA sequencing workflows against explicit criteria. A platform-agnostic study benchmarks four non-fixed single-cell RNA assays (10x, Parse, Scale, Illumina) on human PBMCs, comparing agnostic and platform-specific cell calling. RUVprps is an R package implementing faster RUV-III normalization with pseudo-replicates of pseudo-samples for large RNA-seq datasets, together with assessment metrics. QC-DR visualizes RNA-seq pipeline QC metrics and flags outliers against a reference, with ML models tested on the SCRIPT alveolar macrophage dataset. A separate sample size study estimates median requirements of 190 to 480 samples for binary classification across XGBoost, random forest, and neural networks. Together these items address data generation, normalization, quality control, and study design, though they differ in whether they introduce new software or assess existing practice.
